Home / For therapists

BUILT AROUND YOUR WORKING DAY

More time for care.
Less digital uncertainty.

Email, appointments, video sessions and documents all support your work. A useful review starts with how you use them, not with a demand to replace every tool.

Working on your own?

Start with a short inventory of your business accounts, laptop and phone. Identify who could help if you lost account access or could not reach your appointment schedule.

The planned one-off Practice Security Review provides an inventory and prioritised checklist. It does not require sending client notes.

Explore practice foundations ↗

Sharing a practice?

Include shared accounts, staff joining and leaving, outsourced reception and the division of responsibility between practitioners and IT support.

A scoped account review can clarify permissions and recovery responsibilities. Each account owner must authorise any access.

Explore the account review ↗

Bring your workflow, not your client records

  • Email and newsletters: who signs in, who manages access and how recovery works.
  • Bookings and remote sessions: the services you depend on and how you would handle interruption.
  • Documents and devices: where business information is kept and who manages updates and backups.
  • Existing support: which actions belong to you, your suppliers or your IT provider.
Keep confidential information out of the first conversation.

A list of service names and responsibilities is enough to start. Do not submit patient names, clinical records, passwords or recovery codes.

A proportionate next step

First agree scope, delivery owner, price and availability. Any implementation is agreed separately rather than assumed to be included. A review is not a compliance certificate, and using a particular supplier is not evidence of a weakness.
